nodes.label: ADR-0001: Rust and Cargo Workspace
nodes.rationale: Native cross-platform behavior, low startup and idle overhead, predictable ownership, and independently testable components favor stable Rust and a Cargo workspace.

nodes.label: ADR-0008: License, Naming, and Target Architectures
nodes.norm_label: adr-0008: license, naming, and target architectures
nodes.rationale: The repository needs an open license and explicit native architecture matrix, while branding and OS support floors lack enough implementation evidence for final decisions.

nodes.label: ADR-0007: V1 Scope Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Deferring adjacent IDE and platform features keeps effort focused on terminal correctness, PTY behavior, rendering, and bounded resources.

nodes.label: M2 Typed Cursor and Erase Slice
nodes.norm_label: m2 typed cursor and erase slice

nodes.label: ADR-0002: Component Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Separating terminal semantics, platform I/O, rendering, workspaces, configuration, and orchestration reduces coupled testing and platform-maintenance costs.

nodes.label: ADR-0003: Native Window, Render, and Font Stack
nodes.norm_label: adr-0003: native window, render, and font stack
nodes.rationale: A cross-platform terminal grid needs low-latency rendering, DPI handling, font fallback, and bounded glyph caching without a browser or large GUI framework.

nodes.label: ADR-0004: VTE Parsing with Project-owned State
nodes.norm_label: adr-0004: vte parsing with project-owned state
nodes.rationale: Using vte reduces parser risk while retaining project control over semantics, invariants, resource limits, and testability.

nodes.label: ADR-0005: PTY, Process, and Threading Model
nodes.norm_label: adr-0005: pty, process, and threading model
nodes.rationale: Worker threads prevent blocking the UI while a single-process, bounded, event-driven design avoids premature concurrency complexity.

nodes.label: ADR-0006: Configuration, Commands, and Workspaces
nodes.rationale: Typed configuration and centralized commands keep persistent configuration separate from live state and prevent duplicated behavior across input surfaces.
